text:
alex: noticed dashboards are janky in staging after the last release. heatmaps and metric-panel charts stutter on first paint. FID spikes ~250ms.
maria: saw that too. main chunk up ~350KB after the bundle switch. is the charts lib still being imported eagerly?
jamal: yep, seems like a regression from the telemetry refactor — we pulled `metrics-client` into the top-level app to unify types. probably dragged in moment+d3 deps.
irene: can we confirm with source-map-explorer or bundlebuddy? I can run a quick build-analyze.
alex: ran bundle-analyzer locally: `main.js` now contains `metrics-client`, `d3`, and a new polyfill for Intl. chunk graph attached (will post after). big culprit looks like `metrics-client/index.ts` re-exporting `chart-utils`.
sam: suggestion: lazy-load charts route with `React.lazy()` and dynamic import, or split `chart-utils` into a small runtime-only layer.
maria: dynamic import helps, but dashboard route is still reading a big telemetry payload from `/api/v1/metrics/dashboard` and we wait for it before rendering charts. the network payload is 180KB JSON for a single widget.
jamal: that's the API side change — we started returning precomputed deltas and sample arrays for all scopes to support new rollouts UX. can we make it opt-in per-query? add `fields=summary` or similar.
alex: +1 to making expensive fields opt-in. meanwhile we can early-render placeholders and hydrate charts after fetch to improve Time-to-Interactive.
irene: quick patch idea: split telemetry payload into `meta` and `series` keys, let console request `meta` first. API change should be backwards compatible.
sam: also worth checking CDN cache headers and our edge TTLs. the dashboard JSON is currently `Cache-Control: private, max-age=0` because we added auth caching guard. that prevents edge caching of repeated queries across tenants.
maria: why did auth guard kill edge caching? we have per-user tokens but many calls are identical for org-level dashboards. maybe we can set Vary headers properly and allow org-scoped responses to be cached.
jamal: agree — we can add a cache key that includes `org-id` and keep sensitive fields out of edge-cached payloads.
alex: performance team telemetry shows 40% of chart freezes correlate with large initial JS execution (parse+compile). object shape from API requires deep parsing (lots of arrays). streaming JSON might help.
irene: streaming JSON requires fetch response.body reading and incremental parse. React hydration currently expects full object though.
sam: minimal win: gzip->brotli switch on API and ensuring `transfer-encoding: chunked` with smaller first bytes for meta could shave bytes.
maria: also found a bug where our lazy chunk boundary is broken because `metrics-client` imports `ui-kit/button` which imports global CSS, so chunk can't be separated. need to decouple UI dependencies.
jamal: can we quick-fix by moving CSS imports to entry points and using CSS modules? that will stop accidental cross-chunk coupling.
alex: plan proposal:
1) jamal: expose `fields=summary` on API within 1 day (opt-in expensive arrays)
2) irene: run bundle-split and push a small patch to move metrics-client behind dynamic import in 2 days
3) sam: update CDN caching rules for org-scoped dashboards in a day
4) maria: implement placeholder-first render and hydrating charts async (canary 5% on staging)
5) ops-bot: deploy-bot to do canary rollout and monitor `console.chart_paint_duration` and `bundle.main.size` metrics

maria: tagging metrics to watch: `console.chart_first_paint_ms`, `console.bundle_parse_ms`, `network.dashboard_payload_bytes`.
jamal: also add an SLO alert if 90th percentile chart paint > 2s for more than 5min during rollout.
alex: is anyone opposed to a small revert if canary fails? faster to revert than chase edge cases.
irene: agree — prepare rollback PR and keep current flags open.
sam: one more edge-case: older Safari versions (polyfill added) increase parse time a lot. maybe gate Intl polyfill behind a UA sniff or feature-detect.
maria: I'll prototype the placeholder + async hydrate. pushing PR in ~3hrs.
jamal: I'll add `fields` query and a flag to enable full series on demand by the Console.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: staging canary 5% at 2029-09-15T14:00Z. Rollback window 30m. Monitoring hooks: console.chart_first_paint_ms, console.bundle_main_kb.
deploy-bot: canary started :rocket: — will post results in #eng-sre.
alex: thanks all — hoping we can shave that first paint down and avoid a full revert. :thumbsup:
